en.p21Ask: Tap the correct arc length of this quarter part of the circle.
en.p21WrongQuarter: {f} is one-eighth of the circumference, not one-fourth of it.
en.p21Right: The quadrant is one-fourth of the whole circle.
en.p22Pick: Tap any two points on the circle.
en.p22Central: This is the central angle (θ) for minor sector.
en.p23Right: The two radii meet at the center at an angle of 80°.
en.p23Wrong85: Look where the radius through the second point crosses the inner scale: it is not on the 85° mark.
en.p23Wrong90: At 90° the radius would point straight up from the center. This one leans to the right.
en.p24Ask: What fraction of the whole circle is this sector?
en.p24Right: The whole circle measures 360°, so this sector is 80°⁄360° of it.
en.p24Wrong90: 90° is only a quarter of the circle, not the whole of it.
en.p24Wrong180: 180° is a half turn, so it is only half of the whole circle.
en.p25S: s is the length of the arc.
en.p25Theta: θ is the central angle of the circle.
en.p26Guide: Drag the red point around the circle and watch θ change.
en.p27Ask: Arc length for the central angle 360°?
en.p27Right: A 360° angle goes all the way round, so its arc is the whole circumference, 2πr.
en.p27WrongPiR2: πr² is the area of the circle, not the length of its arc.
en.p27WrongPiR: πr is only half the circumference: the arc of a 180° angle.
en.p29Wrong7: 7 cm is the radius. Look at the angle marked at the centre.
en.p29Wrong180: A half turn is 180°. Look at the angle marked at the centre.
en.p29Wrong14: 14 cm would be the diameter. Look at the radius in the figure.
en.p29Wrong90: 90° is the central angle. Look at the radius in the figure.
en.p29Wrong44: 44 cm is the whole circumference. The arc is only one-fourth of it.
en.p29Wrong22: 22 cm is half of 44 cm. The arc is one-fourth of 44 cm.
en.p30Right: 120° is one-third of 360°, so the arc is one-third of the circumference: 44 cm.
en.p30Wrong66: 66 cm is half the circumference, the arc of a 180° angle. This angle is 120°.
en.p30Wrong132: 132 cm is the whole circumference. The arc is only one-third of it.
en.p31WrongS21: 21 cm is the radius. s is the arc, the length along the rim.
en.p31WrongS42: 42 cm would be the diameter. s is the arc marked on the rim.
en.p31WrongR22: 22 cm is the arc length. r is the radius, from the centre to the rim.
en.p31WrongR42: 42 cm would be the diameter. The radius is half of that.
en.p31Wrong6: One-sixth of 360° is much more than 6°. Divide 360° by 6.
en.p31Wrong30: 360° divided by 6 is not 30°. 30° is one-twelfth of 360°.
en.p32Tip: The tip travels along this arc.
en.p32Right1: The blade length is the radius.
en.p32Right2: The sweep is the central angle.
en.p32WrongChord: The blade turns about one end, so it is a radius, not a chord.
en.p32WrongDiameter: The blade is a radius, not a diameter, and a sweep is an angle, not an area.
en.p33Ask: How much glass is wiped in every sweep?
en.p33Right2: The tip travels 44 cm in every sweep.
en.p33Wrong42: 42 cm is the blade itself, the radius. The tip travels a little further along the arc.
en.p33Wrong48: The whole circumference is 264 cm, and 60° is one-sixth of it: that is not 48 cm.
en.p34Ask: 45 minutes turns the hand through how many degrees?
en.p34Right: 45 minutes is three-quarters of an hour, so the hand turns three-quarters of 360°: 270°.
en.p34Wrong180: 180° is a half turn: the hand does that in 30 minutes, not 45.
en.p34Wrong45: The 45 is minutes, not degrees. The hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, so 45 minutes is far more than 45°.
en.p35Ask: How far does its tip travel in 45 minutes?
en.p35Right2: The tip travels 66 cm in 45 minutes.
en.p35Wrong88: 88 cm is the whole circumference: a full hour. In 45 minutes the tip travels three-quarters of it.
en.p35Wrong44: 44 cm is half the circumference: 30 minutes, not 45.
en.p32Blade1: A wiper blade is 42 cm long.
en.p34Hand1: The minute hand is 14 cm long.
en.a11yClock: A clock face with its minute hand.
en.a11yWindshield: A car windshield, with a wiper blade sweeping across it.
en.a11yDrop: A dropdown. Open it and choose the value.
en.a11ySlot: An empty box for the value to choose.
en.a11yBand: The edge of the circle. Tap it to place a point.
en.a11yProtractor: A protractor laid on the circle, its center on the center of the circle.
en.a11yHandle: The movable end of a radius. Drag it around the circle to change the angle.
